newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmen leader pardons hundreds of prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen leader pardons hundreds of prisoners.

text.p: Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov marked his fifth year in office by pardoning or commuting the sentences of 2,065 prisoners in the desert republic, state television said on Saturday.

"The fate of these people is also the concern of the state," Niyazov told state television on the anniversary of the day he was elected with 99.5 percent of the vote five years ago. "They are also citizens of the republic."
The decree said 222 prisoners who faced the death penalty on drugs trafficking charges would have their sentences commuted to 10 to 20 years in jail.
Most of the traffickers are from the southern Mary region, bordering Afghanistan, the source of much of the drugs trade.

Niyazov, known as Turkmenbashi, or leader of the Turkmens, was the ex-Soviet republic's Communist Party boss and rules the resource-rich state's impoverished population of four million with an iron hand.
"This is not only a holiday for me but for everyone," Niyazov said. "Not only I work but also peasants and workers," he said.

Niyazov is also the focus of an increasingly bizarre personality cult in which his chubby countenance appears on perfume bottles and yoghurt pots along with countless portraits which grace the streets of the capital Ashgabat.
There are plans to build a 70-metre (230-foot) tower near the presidential palace with a 12-metre (40-foot) revolving statue of Niyazov placed on the top.
